name: PHASOR
tagline: RF calculator kit: dBm converter, VSWR and return loss, interactive Smith chart, noise figure cascade and link budget
meta_description: Free RF calculator: dBm/watts/volts converter, VSWR and return loss, interactive Smith chart with L-match solver, Friis noise cascade and link budget.
description:
PHASOR is a pocket toolkit for radio-frequency engineers, students and hobbyists. It brings together the calculations you reach for every day on the bench, and it runs entirely in your browser, with nothing to install and no sign-up.

The Convert tab turns any power or voltage (dBm, dBW, watts, Vrms, Vpk, Vpp, dBµV, dBmV) into all the others at the impedance you choose. Next to it, a mismatch converter moves between VSWR, return loss, reflection coefficient, S11, mismatch loss and reflected power, with a meter showing how much power actually reaches the load.

The Smith tab is an interactive Smith chart. Drag the load point around, or type its resistance and reactance, and PHASOR solves every two-element L-network that matches it to your system impedance. It gives real inductor and capacitor values at your frequency and draws each matching path on the chart.

The Cascade tab works out a receiver chain's total gain, noise figure (Friis), input and output IP3, sensitivity and spurious-free dynamic range. It also shows how much of the total noise each stage contributes. The Link tab builds a free-space link budget with a waterfall chart, fade margin, maximum range and Fresnel-zone radius. Your values are saved on your device.
how_to: Pick a tab: Convert, Smith, Cascade or Link.
Type your values. Every result updates as you type.
On the Smith chart, drag the load point and tap a match solution to see its path.
Tap any result tile to copy its value.
Open the '?' notes under each panel for the formulas behind the numbers.

name: Gyre
tagline: Euclidean rhythm machine: four rings of synthesized drums that spread beats evenly and drift into polyrhythms
meta_description: Free online Euclidean rhythm generator and drum machine. Build polyrhythms with four rotating rings, tresillo and bembé presets, swing and tempo control.
description:
Gyre is a playable Euclidean rhythm machine that runs in your browser. Four concentric rings (hi-hat, chime, snare and kick) each spread a chosen number of hits across a chosen number of steps as evenly as possible. This is the Euclidean algorithm, and it turns out to produce many of the world's traditional rhythms.

Set a ring to 3 hits over 8 steps and you get the Cuban tresillo. 5 over 8 gives the cinquillo, and 7 over 12 gives the West African bembé bell pattern. Give the rings different step counts and they loop at different lengths, so the groove keeps shifting against itself until the cycles line up again. Gyre shows that cycle length in the middle of the dial.

Every sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API, so there are no samples to download. Rotate any ring to shift its pattern, tap individual dots to break the rule, add swing, and save your groove automatically on your device. It's a quick way to explore rhythm theory, find ideas for a beat, or just watch the patterns orbit.
how_to: Press Play (or the space bar) to start the beat.
Pick a preset such as Tresillo, Bembé or Odd 7·9·11, or press Shuffle.
Use each ring's Steps, Hits and Rotate sliders to change its pattern.
Tap any dot on the dial to flip that single step on or off.
Adjust Tempo and Swing, and mute rings to hear the layers.

name: Mycel
tagline: Rotate-the-tiles connection puzzle: turn fungus strands until every mushroom links to the glowing spore
meta_description: Free daily pipe-rotation puzzle game in your browser. Turn the tiles to connect every mushroom to the spore. 5×5, 7×7 and 9×9 boards, daily and random modes.
description:
Mycel is a calm, glowing take on the classic rotate-the-pipes connection puzzle. The board is a patch of forest floor crossed by strands of fungus. A spore sits in the middle, and mushrooms are scattered at the ends of the strands. Every tile has been turned at random, and your job is to rotate them back until every mushroom draws food from the spore.

Tap a tile to turn it a quarter clockwise. Strands that connect back to the spore light up amber, so you can watch the network grow as you solve it. Long-press (or right-click) a tile you're sure of to pin it so you can't turn it by accident. When the last mushroom is fed, a wave of light ripples outward across the board.

Choose a 5×5 Patch, 7×7 Grove or 9×9 Forest. Daily mode gives everyone the same board each day, and Wild mode makes a fresh random board whenever you like. Your best time and move count for each size are saved on your device. There's no sign-up and no ads, and it works on phones and desktops.
how_to: Tap a tile to rotate it clockwise.
Connect strands back to the glowing spore in the middle. Connected strands light up.
Long-press or right-click a tile to pin it in place.
Feed every mushroom to finish the board.
Switch size, or press New for a random Wild board.

name: Lumen
tagline: Laser and mirror puzzle: place mirrors to bend one beam through every crystal
meta_description: Free laser mirror puzzle game in your browser. Place and flip mirrors to bend the beam through every crystal. Endless levels that grow harder, with hints.
description:
Lumen is a laser-and-mirror logic puzzle. A laser fires into the board from the left edge, and somewhere on the grid sit one or more crystals. You have a limited number of mirrors. Place them so the beam bounces around the walls and passes through every crystal, and the crystals light up.

Tap an empty square to drop a mirror, tap again to flip its angle, and tap a third time to remove it. The beam redraws instantly as you go, so you can experiment freely. Walls stop the light, and the counter shows how many mirrors you have left. Any route that lights every crystal counts, so there's often more than one way to solve a board.

Levels start on a small 5×5 board with a single crystal and grow to 9×9 boards with several crystals and more bends. Stuck? Hint locks one correct mirror in place for you. Your progress is saved on your device, so you can come back and carry on. Lumen works on phones and desktops, supports light and dark mode, and needs no account.
how_to: Tap an empty square to place a mirror (╱).
Tap it again to flip it (╲), and once more to remove it.
Route the laser through every crystal using the mirrors you're given.
Use Hint to lock one correct mirror if you're stuck.
Solve the board to unlock the next, larger level.

name: Evolution Sim
tagline: Watch species evolve: an artificial-life simulator with genomes, predators, mating, mutation and speciation
meta_description: Free evolution simulator in your browser. Organisms with genomes eat, hunt, mate and mutate, and new species emerge. Live family tree, charts and CSV export.
description:
Evolution Sim is an artificial-life sandbox where natural selection plays out in front of you. Each organism carries a genome that sets its body size, speed, senses, lifespan and diet. They graze on plants, hunt each other, mate with genetically similar partners and pass on mutated copies of their genes. Nothing about species is scripted: the simulator finds species by clustering genomes, and colours them as they appear.

Over a few minutes you'll see niches form. Plant eaters and meat eaters drift apart, body sizes split, hunters rise and crash with their prey, and lineages branch off and go extinct. A live family tree shows every species over time, a diet-versus-size chart shows the separate niches, and population charts track organisms, hunters and plant biomass. Lifetime stats cover births, deaths by cause, generations and hunting success.

You control the world: its size (up to 3,600 organisms), sim speed or max speed, mutation rate, plant growth, mating range, seasons, and two energy-cost formulas, including a realistic Kleiber-law option. An optional genome layer adds chromosome linkage, regulatory genes and gene duplication. Use a seed to repeat a run exactly, and copy the log as CSV to analyse it yourself.
how_to: Let the simulation run and watch colours (species) appear.
Use the family tree and diet-vs-size charts to see species split into niches.
Change mutation, plant growth or mating range, then press Reset to compare.
Switch on seasons or the genome layer for more complex runs.
Set a seed to repeat a run, and use Copy log as CSV to export data.

docs.title: How the sim evolved and what we observed

name: Tally
tagline: Track anything with counters and timers, nested in groups with roll-up totals and editable history
meta_description: Free habit and time tracker in your browser. Count events or time sessions, nest them in groups with roll-up totals, and browse or edit your history. No sign-up.
description:
Tally is a simple, flexible tracker for anything you want to count or time: dog walks, cups of coffee, practice sessions, meetings, workouts or chores. Each event can be a counter (tap to log one), a timer (start and stop a session) or both.

The twist is that events can be nested. Put "Dog walk" under "Pets", or give each family member their own sub-event, and Tally rolls the totals up the tree, so you see both the detail and the big picture. You can move events to a new parent at any time, and running timers are highlighted so you never forget one.

The History tab shows totals for today, this week, this month or any period, broken down by event. You can edit or delete any entry if you logged something by mistake. Everything is saved privately on your own device. There's no account and no server, and nothing is sent anywhere.
how_to: Open Events and add something to track, choosing counter, timer or both.
Nest events under a parent to get roll-up totals.
On Track, tap +1 to count or Start/Stop to time a session.
Open History to see totals by period and edit any entry.

name: Tincture
tagline: Colour palette generator built on OKLCH, with harmonies, tonal ramps, a WCAG contrast checker and colour-blind previews
meta_description: Free OKLCH colour palette generator: harmonies, 50–950 tonal ramps, WCAG contrast grid, colour-blind simulation and CSS/JSON export. Runs in your browser.
description:
Tincture is a colour-palette studio for designers and front-end developers. It's built on OKLCH, a perceptual colour space where equal steps in lightness actually look equal to the eye. That makes it much easier to build palettes that feel balanced and accessible than working in HSL or hex.

Pick a base colour on the hue disc (hue around the edge, chroma outward), choose a harmony such as complementary, triadic or analogous, and Tincture builds a matching palette. Shuffle to explore and lock the swatches you want to keep. For every colour it generates a full 50 to 950 tonal ramp, like the scales used in Tailwind and modern design systems, spaced evenly in perceived lightness.

A contrast grid shows the WCAG 2 ratio for every text-on-background pair, marked AAA, AA or large-text only, so you can see at a glance which combinations are readable. Colour-blind previews simulate how the palette looks with common types of colour vision deficiency. An in-use preview applies the palette to light and dark surfaces. When you're happy, copy the palette as CSS custom properties or JSON. Everything runs locally in your browser.
how_to: Drag on the hue disc or set L, C and H to choose a base colour.
Pick a harmony, then press Shuffle (or Space) to explore. Lock swatches with 1–5.
Check the tonal ramps and the WCAG contrast grid for readable pairs.
Turn on a colour-blind preview to test accessibility.
Copy the result as CSS variables or JSON from Export.

name: Orbiscribe
tagline: Draw any shape and watch a chain of spinning circles redraw it: Fourier series epicycles, live
meta_description: Interactive Fourier series epicycles drawing toy. Draw any closed shape and watch rotating circles (a discrete Fourier transform) trace it back. Free, in your browser.
description:
Orbiscribe turns any drawing into a chain of spinning circles. Trace a closed shape with your finger or mouse, and Orbiscribe breaks it down with a discrete Fourier transform into circles, each turning at a whole-number speed. Joined tip to tail, they spin together, and the end of the chain redraws your shape.

It's one of the most beautiful ways to see what a Fourier series really does. With only a few circles you get a rough, wobbly outline. As you add more, the tip hugs your line ever more closely, because each extra circle adds a finer level of detail. The largest circles always come first, and a spectrum view shows how much each frequency contributes.

Not in the mood to draw? Try the built-in shapes: a heart, a star, a trefoil, a square or the π symbol. You can change the number of circles and the speed, show or hide the circles and the original drawing, and pause to study a single moment. It's a great classroom demo for Fourier analysis, signal processing or complex numbers, and a mesmerising toy for anyone else.
how_to: Draw one continuous closed shape on the canvas, or pick a preset shape.
Watch the spinning circles redraw it.
Use the Circles slider to add or remove circles and see the fit change.
Adjust Speed, and toggle the circles or the original line.
Check the Spectrum to see how strong each frequency is.

name: Heliograph
tagline: Sun path and daylight explorer: sunrise, sunset, golden hour, blue hour and shadow length for any place and day
meta_description: Free sun path calculator: sunrise, sunset, golden and blue hour, sun altitude, shadow length and a year-long daylight map for any location and date.
description:
Heliograph shows where the sun is in the sky for any place on Earth, on any day of the year. Use your location or enter one, and it draws the sun's path across the sky, its height above the horizon through the day, and the exact times of sunrise, sunset and solar noon.

It's built for photographers, gardeners, architects and the simply curious. Golden hour and blue hour are marked so you can plan a shoot. The shadow-length readout tells you how long the shadow of a pole or building will be at any moment, which helps with garden beds, solar panels and room lighting. Civil, nautical and astronomical twilight are shown too, for stargazers.

The year view is a daylight map: every day of the year on one chart, coloured by high sun, golden hour, twilight and night. You can see at a glance how day length changes through the seasons. Tap or drag on it to jump to any day and time, or press Play to animate the sun across a day. All calculations run in your browser using standard solar-position formulas, and your location is never sent anywhere.
how_to: Press Locate to use your location, or set a place.
Pick a day and drag the time to move the sun.
Read sunrise, sunset, golden hour and shadow length.
Press Play day to animate the sun's path.
Tap the year map to jump to any day and time.

name: Dahdit
tagline: Learn Morse code by ear: a tappable telegraph key, a Koch-method trainer, a translator and a sounding chart
meta_description: Free Morse code trainer and translator. Learn by ear with the Koch method, tap a telegraph key that decodes your sending, and translate text to Morse audio.
description:
Dahdit is a complete Morse code toolkit that teaches you to hear code, not count dots. It's named after the rhythm of the letter D: dah-di-dit.

The Learn tab uses the Koch method, the approach many radio amateurs swear by. You start with just two characters played at full speed, tap the letter you heard, and a new character is added each time you reach 90% accuracy. Farnsworth timing lets you keep each character fast while adding extra space between them, so you learn the sound of letters rather than counting beeps.

The Key tab turns your screen (or the space bar) into a telegraph key. Tap for a dit, hold for a dah, and Dahdit decodes what you send in real time, adapting to your speed and showing your WPM. The Translate tab turns any text into Morse code and plays it as audio, and the Chart tab lets you tap any character to hear it. You can set character speed, effective speed, tone pitch and volume. It follows the international Morse standard (ITU-R M.1677) and runs entirely in your browser.
how_to: Open Learn and press Start, then tap the letter you heard.
Reach 90% accuracy to unlock the next character.
Use Key to practise sending: tap for a dit, hold for a dah.
Type text in Translate and press Play to hear it.
Adjust speed, tone and volume in Settings.
